learning: If line_loss_events fall to zero and max_error drops below 0.06 m, the sensing change is the fix. If line loss stays at zero but max_error is still above 0.06 m, the limit is turn authority; check the controller signal and kp. If steering_oscillation exceeds about 0.25, restore y to 0.04 m and reduce kp toward 6.0.
notes: Complete robot for the Builder's sensor_size 0.016 m, y = 0.03 m geometry, with the iteration 2 drivetrain and controller held. Compare per track against iteration 2.
rationale: Iteration 2 (score 74.95) left max_error at 0.063 to 0.064 m on all three tracks, just above the 0.06 m floor, and line loss at 1.0 (oval, s-bend) and 1.9 (slalom). Widening the span to seven sensors (iteration 1) did not remove line loss, so the Builder's sensing change is a valid next test. The Builder's iteration 3 geometry keeps the seven x positions, sets sensor_size to 0.016 m (so each footprint covers more of the 25 mm tape at the edges) and moves the forward row to y = 0.03 m (shorter look-ahead, with iteration 2 oscillation at 0.18 to 0.20, well under the 0.25 limit). I keep the iteration 2 controller unchanged (kp 7.0, ki 0.2, kd 0.3, base_speed 1.8, last_direction, weights x/0.018), so the only changes in the race are the two sensing parameters. The weights remain valid for the seven x positions, and the sensor row position does not change the signal scale. I expect line_loss_events to fall toward zero and max_error to move toward 0.06 m. The controller does not need retuning for this step; I will adjust kp only if the next race shows oscillation or saturation.
